name: Starter: Latvian
about: Latvian cases and word order in real, everyday sentences.

words.būt: to be (ir: is; nav: isn't, there's no)
words.braukt: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.iet: to go (on foot) (kā tev iet: how are you)
words.saukt: to call (kā tevi sauc: what's your name)
words.patikt: to please (man patīk: I like it)
words.pēc: after; for (pēc maizes: to get bread)
words.par: too (par mazu: too small); about, for
words.pie: at or to someone's (pie vecmāmiņas: to grandma's)
words.kino: the movies, movie theater (uz kino: to the movies)
words.auksts: cold (auksti: of the weather or how someone feels)
words.dot: to give (dod ziņu: let me know)
words.ziņa: message; news (dod ziņu: let me know)

es-veletos.about: A polite way to order or ask for something: Es vēlētos kafiju.

ka-tev-iet.about: The everyday how are you, literally how does it go to you; often answered Labi (fine).

ka-tevi-sauc.about: Literally how do they call you; politely, Kā jūs sauc?

dod-zinu.about: Literally give a message; to more than one, or politely, Dodiet ziņu.

rekinu-ludzu.about: The usual way to ask for the bill in a café or restaurant.

skaidra-nauda.about: Literally clear money; Man nav skaidras naudas is I don't have any cash.

kaut-ko.about: Something, anything, as one piece: kaut ko saldu (something sweet).

nedelas-nogale.about: nedēļas nogale is the weekend (the week's end), and nedēļas nogalē is on the weekend.

atvainojiet.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry: polite, or to more than one; one friend gets Atvaino.

items.text: Vienu tēju un vienu ūdeni, lūdzu.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Viens tēju un vienu ūdeni, lūdzu.
Vienu tēju un vienu ūdens, lūdzu.

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.
Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Excuse me, how much is it?
I live in a small house.
My mom goes to the city.
Tomorrow I'm going to the city.

items.text: Man ir viena māsa un divi brāļi.
items.means: I have one sister and two brothers.
wrong: Es ir viena māsa un divi brāļi.
Man ir viena māsa un divas brāļi.

items.means: I don't know where he lives.
wrong: Es ne zinu, kur viņš dzīvo.

items.means: My mom works at a hospital.
I live in a small apartment.
There's a book on the table.
There's no milk in the fridge.

items.text: Mums ir liela virtuve un mazs balkons.
items.means: We have a big kitchen and a small balcony.
wrong: Mums ir lielu virtuvi un mazu balkonu.
Mums ir liels virtuve un mazs balkons.

items.means: When I get home, I'll make dinner.
I'd like a glass of water.
I want to eat something sweet.

items.text: Man patīk gatavot kopā ar mammu.
items.means: I like cooking with my mom.
wrong: Man patīk gatavot kopā ar mamma.

items.means: I'm going to the store for bread.

items.means: Tomorrow I'll go to work by bus.
wrong: Rīt uz darbu braukšu ar autobuss.

items.means: The train was ten minutes late.
The new shoes are too small.
Grandma's waiting for us at the station.

items.means: Are you coming to the movies with us?
wrong: Vai nāksi ar mēs uz kino?

items.means: We're going to the beach this weekend.
I've been learning Latvian for a year.

wrong: Ceru, ka rīt būs laba laiks.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person: (es) dzīvoju, (tu) dzīvo, (viņš, viņa) dzīvo, (mēs) dzīvojam, (jūs) dzīvojat, (viņi) dzīvo; to be is esmu, esi, ir, esam, esat, ir.
A yes/no question usually starts with vai (Vai tu runā angliski?), and a question word like kur, ko or kā usually starts its question; Latvian adds no do.

words.means: esmu = am; esi = are; neesmu = am not

concept.line: Every noun is masculine (often -s, -š or -is: brālis, galds) or feminine (often -a or -e: mamma, virtuve), and the words with it match: mans brālis, mana mamma.
Latvian has no words for a, an or the; context does their work: Esmu skolotājs; Uz galda ir grāmata.

words.means: nesaprotu = do not understand; saproti = understand

concept.line: The accusative marks the direct object (Dzeru kafiju; Pagaidi mani), and in the singular follows uz for where you're going: uz veikalu, uz darbu, uz pludmali.

words.means: māja = house; mājā = in a house
maza = small; mazā = in a small

concept.line: The dative is to or for someone (Piezvanīšu tev), the one who feels or likes (Man ir auksti: I'm cold; Man patīk: I like it), and after most prepositions in the plural: ar mums, ar draugiem.

words.means: jāiet = must go; iet = to go
